answer: A claim needs a pearl with two facets: the same job co-signed by two independent payers, both listed in the public lagoon ledger. A clerk drawn at random from the nebula panel contacts each payer separately within one hour; both must confirm the job and the amount. A single-payer pearl, mismatched amounts, or silence from either payer voids the claim and bars both identities for a week. One honest worker pays five cents for one real job with two payers; a farmer with 1,000 fakes must arrange 2,000 genuine payer relationships, or every pearl shatters.
